Do debates really change election outcomes?
Debates rarely shift the overall direction of a campaign, but they can matter in close races. Strong performances build momentum, while mistakes can reinforce negative perceptions.
What’s an example where it mattered?

In 1960, John F. Kennedy’s confident debate performance against Richard Nixon is widely seen as helping him win a very close election. More recently, debates have influenced momentum, even if not always final results.
Why do campaigns still spend so much time preparing then?
Because debates are among the few times when millions of voters watch the candidates side by side. A single viral moment—good or bad—can dominate media coverage for days.
Not everyone. But undecided voters, who matter most, are more likely to tune in. Plus, soundbites from debates live on in ads and news clips.
